newsitem.title: INDIA: India Congress tells deputies to vote out PM - PTI.
newsitem.headline: India Congress tells deputies to vote out PM - PTI.

text.p: India's Congress party on Thursday ordered its lawmakers in parliament to vote against Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda in a confidence motion on Friday, the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

"All Congress members of (the lower house of parliament) are requested to be present without fail, cancelling all their other engagements of whatever importance or urgency they might be on tomorrow, defeat the motion of confidence and support the party stand," PTI quoted the text of the Congress order as saying.
"They should remain present in the house from 11 a.m. (0530 GMT) throughout the day, till the motion is defeated," the order said.

The move followed a second round of talks between representatives of the ruling United Front and Congress earlier on Thursday. On Wednesday the Congress unsuccessfully demanded its party chief Sitaram Kesri be made prime minister.
The Congress party withdrew its make-or-break support to Deve Gowda on March 30, citing a drift in the economy and alleged failure to check communalism.
